flashcards.q: What breaks vs survives under quantum attacks?
flashcards.a: Breaks: RSA, DH, ECDH, ECDSA/EdDSA (Shor). Survives weakened: AES (halve strength: use AES-256), SHA-384, HMAC. TLS cipher suites are symmetric and survive; only key-exchange groups die.

flashcards.q: The three finalized NIST PQC standards?
flashcards.a: FIPS 203 ML-KEM (from CRYSTALS-Kyber, lattice KEM), FIPS 204 ML-DSA (from CRYSTALS-Dilithium, lattice signatures), FIPS 205 SLH-DSA (SPHINCS+, hash-based) - all published August 13, 2024.
FN-DSA (Falcon) in development as FIPS 206; HQC selected March 11, 2025 (NIST IR 8545) as code-based KEM backup - algorithm diversity against future cryptanalysis.
Public key 1184 B, ciphertext 1088 B, shared secret 32 B; operations run in tens of microseconds on modern CPUs - faster than RSA private-key operations.
ML-DSA-65: pk 1952 B, sig 3309 B vs EdDSA's 64 B. JWTs balloon, cert chains add tens of KB; consider opaque short-lived tokens with signing only at issuance.
Adversaries record encrypted traffic today and decrypt after a CRQC exists; any data needing confidentiality past ~2033 is at risk NOW. Drives KEM-first migration regardless of hardware timelines.

flashcards.q: Why migrate key exchange before signatures?
flashcards.a: KEM traffic is retroactively vulnerable (HNDL) so urgency is now; signatures have no retroactive theft risk but rotate slowest (root CAs, HSMs, firmware) - inventory immediately, deploy 2027-2033.

flashcards.q: Hybrid key exchange definition and rationale?
flashcards.a: X25519MLKEM768 computes both classical and PQC secrets, mixing them into the TLS key schedule: secure unless BOTH break. Protects against new-scheme implementation/analysis risk during transition.
New NSS acquisitions CNSA 2.0-compliant from January 2027; software/firmware signing exclusive 2030; web/cloud/OS/custom apps exclusive by 2033.
Initial Public Draft (as of Aug 2026): proposes deprecating RSA-2048/ECC-P256 around 2030, disallowing entirely by 2035. Plan against them but cite as draft, not law.

flashcards.q: Why did SIKE and Rainbow dying matter?
flashcards.a: Both competition finalists broke via CLASSICAL attacks (Castryck-Decru 2022, Beullens 2022): proves 'not RSA' isn't a security proof and justifies hybrid deployment plus algorithm diversity.

flashcards.q: First three moves of a PQC migration program?
flashcards.a: 1) Automated crypto inventory (CBOM) wired into CI, 2) data-longevity classification under HNDL lens, 3) enable X25519MLKEM768 on external endpoints with handshake-failure telemetry.
>50% of human Cloudflare web traffic on X25519MLKEM768 (Oct 2025); OpenSSL >=3.5 native ML-KEM (Apr 2025); Signal PQXDH (2023); iMessage PQ3 (2024); FIPS 140-2 certificates historical since Sep 2026.
